WK01.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production sprite atlas for an original hand-painted 2D military science-fiction side-scrolling game, ORDRE DE CENDRE.
Make a SQUARE image with EXACTLY sixteen isolated modular mechanical parts, strictly laid out on an invisible regular FOUR COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS grid, equal square cells. True transparent alpha background everywhere outside each object. Each part is centered inside its own cell, generous transparent padding, no overlap across cells, no grid lines, no captions, absolutely no lettering or numbers. The rows below describe exact reading order, left to right.
Style: sophisticated hand-painted game sprites, precise readable silhouette, matte angular replaceable armor panels, worn dark steel, visible bolts and hinges, restrained chips and rust, small warm amber cockpit glazing. Orthographic SIDE view, facing RIGHT. Flat side projection with subtle surface shading, NOT isometric or three-quarter perspective. Soft upper-left illumination, no external cast shadow, no ground, no decorative effects.
ROW 1: [1] intact cockpit/body HULL ONLY; [2] the SAME hull visibly battle-damaged, dents, exposed small internal panels, outline and mount locations preserved; [3] the SAME hull with its built-in mechanical locking latches visibly engaged, same footprint and silhouette; [4] separate horizontal gun and circular gun cradle, pivot circle on the LEFT, straight barrel pointing RIGHT, muzzle and pivot center on one horizontal axis.
ROW 2: [1] upper leg segment, horizontal LEFT-to-RIGHT bar with round mounting sockets at both ends; [2] IDENTICAL upper segment with localized damaged armor and exposed steel, intact end sockets at same positions; [3] lower leg segment, horizontal LEFT-to-RIGHT bar with round end sockets; [4] IDENTICAL lower segment with localized damage, same endpoints.
ROW 3: [1] isolated circular HIP rotary joint disk, flat side view; [2] isolated circular KNEE rotary joint disk, flat side view; [3] a single wide armored FOOT, flat sole perfectly horizontal, ankle receiver at top center; [4] identical FOOT with localized damage, same contact sole.
ROW 4: [1] identical FOOT in braced state with integrated cleats/locks engaged but same width and same flat contact sole, no extending outriggers; [2] a single tall rectangular ribbed RADIATOR heat exchanger panel with short fittings; [3] identical radiator damaged and soot-stained with bent fins; [4] identical radiator repaired with a neat patch and a few brighter new fins.
Critical mechanical invariants: the three HULLS are detached cabin/body only, NO legs, NO feet, NO cannon, NO external radiator, NO turret mount circle baked into the hull. Leave broad central flank armor available for an independently overlaid gun pivot. Damage/brace states preserve proportions, angle, center and outer footprint. Upper/lower segments are straight horizontal assemblies, both endpoint socket centers on the SAME horizontal axis. NO bent entire leg, NO hoses or pistons bridging across separate parts. Joints are CIRCLES, not ellipses. All three radiator panels have matching outline. Each part fully contained in its cell; detached objects only. No duplicated whole walker. No smoke, no sparks, no painted ground shadow. All sixteen cells occupied with exactly the listed object.
Chassis identity: WK01 VIGIE M-12, a tall two-legged scout walker. Ochre/tan armor (#d5ad72) over charcoal steel with restrained pale-ivory edge markings and copper fittings. Hull: relatively high angular forward cockpit on the RIGHT, compact reinforced rear on the LEFT, chest-like raised roof, small thin antenna, roughly 1.75 times as wide as its main armored body is tall; no humanoid head or arms. Upper and lower leg bars are long slender structural beams with distinct protected internal hydraulic rails and modest ochre armor covers. The foot is a broad low trapezoidal steel shoe. The gun has a compact ochre circular cradle, reinforced straight black-steel barrel and modest block muzzle, roughly four times as long as its maximum height. Radiators are portrait aspect, roughly twice as tall as wide. This is a coherent original industrial family, no existing franchise design.
